description: The Title 17 process to become an authorized service provider for the Regional Center.

sections.title: Vendor Application & Program Design
sections.summary: Align your facility with the Regional Center's specific needs and service levels.

bullets.label: Submit Vendor Application (Form DS 1890)
bullets.detail: This is the 'Golden Ticket.' You must submit this to the specific Regional Center in whose catchment area your home is located.

bullets.label: Finalize the Program Design
bullets.detail: A detailed document (often 30-50 pages) describing your service model, staffing ratios, and how you will meet the needs of Regional Center consumers.

bullets.label: Determine Service Level (1-4)
bullets.detail: Your rate is determined by the level of care (Level 2, 3, or 4A-I). Higher levels require more specialized staffing and more intensive Program Designs.

sections.title: Rate Setting & Electronic Billing
sections.summary: Establishing the financial pipeline for monthly reimbursements.

bullets.label: Sign the Vendor Agreement
bullets.detail: Once approved, you receive a unique Vendor Number. This contract binds you to Title 17 regulations, including strict reporting of 'Special Incidents' (SIRs).

bullets.label: Setup e-Billing (e-Billing System)
bullets.detail: Most California Regional Centers use the EDI/e-Billing portal. You will need to learn the 'Attendance' and 'Invoice' submission workflow to get paid.

sections.title: Placement & Ongoing Monitoring
sections.summary: Moving from an empty house to a fully staffed residential facility.

bullets.label: Host the Facility Liaison Visit
bullets.detail: The Regional Center Liaison will visit your home to verify it matches your Program Design before they send the first 'Referral Packet' for a resident.

bullets.label: Execute Admission Agreements
bullets.detail: This is the contract between the Licensee, the Resident, and the Regional Center. It must comply with both Title 22 and Title 17 standards.
